title: The Bone Orchard — outside the north gate of Sill
caption: The burial ground a league north of the Cross, drawn at walking scale along the north gate road: the rough-staked ground of the thin-return children's shallow graves, the east ground where pots are broken for the dead and left where they fell, the barrow of grey Ash that goes out through the north gate on every market-day and comes back empty, and the road running on through the gate to Cold Acre on the ridge with its six houses, its barley and turnips and its well that never freezes. The north bridge, the Ilm and Sill are drawn faint at the foot for neighbourhood only. Cartouche dated Y.H. 813, the month of Ember, with compass, a league scale in paces, a convention of signs and surveyor's notes on the barrow, the unslated graves, the pots broken for the house and the road that is clay to the ankle in Silt. An engraved broken pot in the margin.
